tail.basis: Editorial declining tail, age = 50 + floor(-scale * ln(1-u)) truncated to max_age; not a fitted mortality model. Review scales 8 and 16 before adoption.

forager.era: Mobile foraging analogues; extrapolation into prehistory has low confidence.

early_farmer.era: Local transition to food production; no universal calendar cutoff.

agrarian.era: Established pre-modern rural agrarian populations; English early-modern records are a regional anchor only.

urban.era: Pre-sanitation towns and cities; London 1650–1799 is an anchor, not an ancient-world table.

GK2007.citation: Gurven and Kaplan (2007), Longevity Among Hunter-Gatherers, Population and Development Review 33(2), 321–365.

BA2011.citation: Bocquet-Appel (2011), When the world's population took off, Science 333, 560–561.
BA2011.locator: Abstract; relative fertility change, not absolute age shares.

LANDERS1987.citation: Landers (1987), London's mortality in the long eighteenth century, Medical History Supplement 11, 1–28.
LANDERS1987.locator: Table 10 and accompanying England comparison tables.

EDITORIAL2026.locator: Prior construction and limitations; all age-share values and envelopes are editorial scenarios.
